spool_path.description: Root path of the news spool directory.

etc_path.description: Path to the INN configuration directory.

bin_path.description: Path to the INN binary executables.

lock_path.description: Path to the lock files directory.

run_path.description: Path to the runtime PID files directory.

log_path.description: Path to the INN log files directory.

hostname.description: Fully qualified hostname of this INN server, used in Message-IDs.

mailhost.description: Mail domain to append to short hostnames when generating Message-IDs.

max_article_body.description: Maximum size (in bytes) of an article body. Set to 0 for unlimited.

max_article_count.description: Maximum number of articles in the spool (0 = unlimited).

max_threads.description: Maximum number of active threads the server will track.

max_connections_per_ip.description: Maximum simultaneous INN connections allowed per client IP.

max_incoming.description: Maximum number of simultaneous incoming (NNTP) connections.

max_outgoing.description: Maximum number of simultaneous outgoing (peer) connections.

local_only.description: If true, only accept local (non-networked) connections — no incoming feeds.

log_incoming.description: If true, log all incoming connections and commands.

log_outgoing.description: If true, log all outgoing connections and transfers.

log_storage.description: If true, log article storage operations.

log_errors.description: If true, log all errors and warnings to the error log.

peers.description: List of peer news servers for feed exchange.

host.description: Hostname or IP of the peer server.

user.description: Optional INN user account name to use for authentication to this peer.

allowed_ips.description: List of IP ranges (CIDR notation) allowed to connect as INN clients.

auto_groups.description: List of newsgroups to create automatically at startup.

moderated.description: If true, group is moderated (newsgroup.{{name}} line will set 'y' flag).

storage_path.description: Directory for storage backend files (applies only to file-based storage methods).
